mathematical_model.name: Thompson Cartesian transformation (method of co-ordinates), formalised as a smooth planar map
mathematical_model.state_variables: x = (x, y): position of a homologous anatomical point in the human reference frame (Fig. 404 grid units, 1 unit = 1 cell); x' = T(x) in the target species' frame

equations.E1_whole_diagram_map: x' = T(x) = A x + t + sum_k w_k U(|x - p_k|), U(r) = r^2 log r (thin-plate spline through the digitised net nodes p_k -> p'_k; T is C^1 and the unique minimiser of the bending energy among interpolants)
equations.E2_affine_part: A = [[a11,a12],[a21,a22]]; the 'rectangular box stretch' null is a11>0, a22>0, a12=a21=0
equations.E3_bending_energy: J[T] = integral (T_xx^2 + 2 T_xy^2 + T_yy^2) dx dy = (1/8 pi) w^T K w  (0 iff T is affine)
equations.E4_cell_area_ratio: lambda(i,j) = Area(T(cell_ij)) / Area(cell_ij)  (shoelace on the 4 digitised node corners); Thompson's 'approximately logarithmic order' <=> log lambda(i,j) ~ alpha + beta_i i + beta_j j with beta_i > 0 (behind->forwards), beta_j < 0 (above->downwards)
equations.E5_procrustes_distance: d_P(X,Y) = min_{s,R,t} || (X - cX)/|X - cX| - s R (Y - cY)/|Y - cY| - t ||_F  (full Procrustes, 2D)
equations.E6_explained_fraction: E = 1 - d_P(T(H), C) / d_P(H, C): fraction of the human->target shape distance removed by applying Thompson's drawn transformation T to the human landmarks H (C = real target landmarks)
equations.E7_facial_proportions: F = |NAS-PRO| / |NAS-OPC| (face projection : braincase length); facial angle phi = angle between PRO->NAS and the Frankfort line ORBI->POR; Thompson: phi -> ~90 deg in man

mathematical_model.boundary_conditions: T is defined on the human bounding box [0,5] x [0,4] (Fig. 404); the net nodes of Fig. 405 are Dirichlet data; outside the box T is the TPS extrapolation

tps_regularisation_lambda.meaning: 0 = exact interpolation of the drawn net; large = affine-only limit (box stretch)

deformation_intensity_k.meaning: T_k = Id + k (T - Id): k=0 human, k=1 Thompson's chimpanzee net, k>1 Thompson's 'increased intensity' baboon hypothesis

fig404_grid_pixels.method: ink projection peaks on fig404_human_skull_cartesian.jpg (crop of leaf 789 box x600-1460,y800-1500)

fig405_chimpanzee_net_nodes_px.method: Otsu ink mask -> remove thick label glyphs -> skeletonize -> degree>=3 skeleton junctions clustered (r=6 px); the four boundary corners (0,0),(0,d),(5,d),(5,0) are L-corners, not junctions, and were read manually at 4x zoom (+/-3 px)
fig405_chimpanzee_net_nodes_px.node_order: rows = ordinate level 0,a,b,c,d (bottom to top in Fig. 404); columns = abscissa 0..5 (back to front); pixel y increases downward

definitions: PRO
prosthion: most anterior-inferior point of the upper alveolar process between the central incisors
NAS
nasion: midline frontonasal junction / deepest point of the nasal root in profile
RHI
rhinion: anterior-inferior tip of the nasal bones (top of the bony nasal aperture)
ORBS
supraorbitale: highest point of the lateral orbital margin
ORBI
orbitale: lowest point of the lateral orbital margin
VTX
vertex (Type-II pseudo-landmark): vault-outline point farthest from the chord PRO-OPC
OPC
opisthocranion (Type-II pseudo-landmark): posterior-outline point farthest from PRO
POR
porion: uppermost point of the external auditory meatus
GON
gonion: angle of the mandible (most posterior-inferior point of the ramus-corpus junction)
GNA
gnathion: most anterior-inferior point of the mandibular symphysis
MPOST
distal end of the upper post-canine tooth row (posterior-most visible upper molar)
landmark_protocol.digitiser: loop agent (claude-fable-5.1) reading 25-50 px coordinate overlays at 1.3-1.6x zoom; NOT an expert osteologist
landmark_protocol.uncertainty_note: propagated by the jitter bootstrap in the script (sigma = 1.5% centroid size ~ 10-15 px)

empirical_claims_to_test.claim: Thompson's drawn human->chimpanzee net (Fig. 405), applied to the human skull landmarks of Fig. 404, moves them toward a real chimpanzee skull
empirical_claims_to_test.metric: E6 explained fraction E_C > 0 (bootstrap CI excludes 0), and T(H) closer to real chimp than the affine-only (box-stretch) fit of the drawn net

empirical_claims_to_test.claim: cell areas of the chimpanzee net increase in approximately logarithmic order from above downwards and from behind forwards
empirical_claims_to_test.metric: R^2 of log lambda(i,j) on (i,j) >= 0.8 with beta_i > 0 and beta_j < 0

empirical_claims_to_test.claim: chimpanzee nearer to human than baboon; dog farther still
empirical_claims_to_test.metric: d_P(H,C) < d_P(H,B) < d_P(H,D) on real specimens

empirical_claims_to_test.claim: baboon transformation is of the same order as chimpanzee's, only more intense
empirical_claims_to_test.metric: cosine between the H->C and H->B Procrustes displacement fields >= 0.8 and best-fit intensity k_B/k_C > 1

empirical_claims_to_test.claim: dog deformation is on different lines (not an intensified ape transformation)
empirical_claims_to_test.metric: cosine(H->C, H->D) < cosine(H->C, H->B); dog taper index (anterior/posterior silhouette height) lowest

empirical_claims_to_test.claim: facial/cranial proportions: face enlarges and facial angle falls from man to apes
empirical_claims_to_test.metric: F_H < F_C < F_B and phi_H > phi_C > phi_B on real specimens

camper_facial_angle_deg.Homo sapiens: 70-80 (Camper 1791 range ~70-80; modern crania ~80-85 with Frankfort reference)
camper_facial_angle_deg.source: textbook ranges; used only as a sanity band, not as a fitted target

biological_reference_values_literature.note: No published 2D lateral landmark table for exactly Homo/Pan/Papio/Canis with these 11 landmarks was found in the open literature during scouting; the Commons specimens are therefore the empirical reference.
